Default.tutOverviewText:
At the start of each round, each player is assigned a unique rank between 1 and 8. Each player starts with a Gun and draws 2 action cards from the deck.

On your turn, you can play any card in your hand except the Gun. Each card will either be "used" (if your rank is one of the numbers at the top of the card) or "failed" (if your rank is one of the numbers on the side of the card). If your card is used, your immediately take the action written on the card.

When it is NOT your turn, you may use your Gun within the first 10 seconds of the current player's turn. The first player to use their Gun shoots a player of their choice, ending the round.
Default.tutActionCardsText: Any action card you play will go in the center board in the deck with your name on it. Cards that were failed show a red X on them.
Default.tutRanksText: The game tracks the possible ranks that each player could have - look at the labels of each deck in the center. A label like "146" means this player could either have a rank of 1, 4, or 6 based on all the cards that have been played so far. A player is publicly revealed if they have just 1 possible rank.
Default.tutScoringText:
Each player's goal is shoot the player with the highest rank that isn't them. This means most players are trying to shoot the player with the highest rank, while the player with the highest rank is trying to shoot the player with the second-highest rank. The player with the highest rank can also win if the Draw Deck runs out of cards.

A successful shot earns you 1 point. An unsuccessful shot earns every other player 1 point. If you shoot successfully, you can also earn an additional point by having at least 1 Inform card in your hand.
Default.tutRoundsText: Spy Noir is played over multiple rounds until one player reaches a certain number of points based on the player count.
Default.tutWinnerText:
Players accumulate points over multiple rounds, and can choose when to end the game. The winner is the player with the most points.

The game will automatically ends when a player reaches 5 points (3-player game), 4 points (4-player game), or 3 points (5/6-player game).
Default.tutNoActionText: On your turn, if you do not play a card in time, choose a player in time, etc., a random valid action will be taken for you.
